page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-16GB is a KVM-based virtual server featuring 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, translating to a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. This configuration utilizes a shared CPU allocation model with 4 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. It includes 16 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, but lacks local storage and GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results present a mixed performance profile. The server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2310.0 and a top-tier text processing score of 3183.0. However, multi-core and raw compute benchmarks are more modest; stress-ng single-core performance is in the bottom 10%, and multi-core performance is in the bottom 25%. Memory performance also varies, with small-block read-only bandwidth reaching an average 410.01 GB/sec, while large-block write bandwidth falls into the bottom 10% at 14.27 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of bundled local storage, this server offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that require moderate, bursty CPU resources rather than sustained, high-throughput multi-core execution. It is well-suited for general-purpose tasks such as text processing, lightweight web serving, software compilation, and running small language model inference. It is less optimal for memory-intensive database operations or high-throughput static web serving due to its lower multi-core and write bandwidth performance.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-16GB is an x86_64 virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor, featuring 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation, it provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The hardware lacks local storage and GPU accelerators but includes 16 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX and AES instructions. Performance benchmarks reveal a dual nature: the server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, yet exhibits weaker multi-core compute and large-block memory write speeds. This profile makes it a cost-efficient option for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, and light text or image processing, while it remains less suited for intensive database operations or high-throughput static web serving.
